Where you nearly get to know yourself,

You are not what happened
To you;

author: john_keats

text: Burial is by no means as bad as death, though it be worse than both for those who are left behind; for there can be nothing sadder than to see those that you love taken away from your sight and then buried away forever out of view. But what will I say about burial? It has been said before: 'To bury someone is not hard.' Burial may bring forth sadness but if we think back on how much grief was caused by this person's death, such things will seem small compared with the suffering they have endured through their life.

James Baldwin was an American author who wrote about the experiences of African-Americans during and after World War II. His most famous works include Go Tell it on the Mountain (1953), Giovanni's Room (1856) and The Fire Next Time (1057). In his book “The Fire Next time,” he describes his experience as a gay man living in Paris, where homosexuality is illegal.

But before she had reached her destination, another came along; this one sang louder than ever—and we all knew what was coming next! author: john_keats
text:
A little bee buzzed
Round my peach blossoms,
As I stood gazing at
The stately castle
Built upon the sea shore.
All alone it stands there
In its grandeur and beauty;
So tall is it’s structure
That no one could see
Any other buildings nearby!

author: john_masefield
text:
"Mother's Walk Down by the Mill."

Where I grew up by the water,
My father was working there;
He had a job that required him
To go along each morning.

So I'd play all day long
In my old, abandoned house;
The birds were singing songs,
And Mother she walked out at noon.

In the world that is black and white,

While you go out there to fight.

You are strong as an elephant

And my mother was so proud!

Merchants, who are generally much addicted to gambling and gaming, must not be admitted into that company of gentlemen which is to be formed for promoting good order and morals among such as are more addicted to vice than to virtue; but those whom I am speaking of are not like them. I will not feed thee, O thou cursed man!

I will strip you bare and let your limbs hang;

Then I'll cut your head from your shoulders off.

Your body into pieces I'd rather lop.

author: robert_frost
text:
The way it is to go, my lady;

So be it! 'Tis all one

To me: for what have I, or know?


I am too old now to change:

Too blind now to see, and poor

Now that my days are gone by.

That echoed through the vales and woods,
Which made each heart with joy beat higher,

Is hushed, unheard for evermore !

text: In this line (1), "little" modifies "birds", and it's an adjective. In lines 2-4, "musing" is an infinitive phrase. The gerund "sat" follows the subject "little birds" ("Little birds sat musing."). In line 5, the prepositional phrase "(a) man passed nearby" tells us where the action occurred; the verb "did" doesn't modify anything because it isn't describing any action or movement. The last two lines are incomplete sentences, but they do contain useful information about what was going on

author: thomas_hardy

The world has moved on, I see; and now the sea
Is calm, while once it was a tempest’s seat ;
And round about that old dismantled town
Where he who died upon the cross is crowned.

But yet a voice from yonder broken tower
Goes up to heaven, and calls the wind her mate :
She hears him answer with a breathless groan,
As when one dead would call another down!

"The Universe in Union," Lo ! here
the Magnet of creation hides;
All distance toward it ever more
admires.
Sweet attraction in it resides,
such as we seek from afar.
Communion sweet by its tide inspires,
a finer bond than human ties!
